extracted.intended_audience: postsecondary institution Title IX coordinators, decision-makers, investigators, administrators, and legal counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements for postsecondary institutions' Title IX grievance processes, with emphasis on live hearings, advisor participation, evidence rules, confidentiality, and remedial obligations to ensure impartial, reliable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective evaluation of all relevant evidence and equal treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must objectively evaluate all relevant evidence (inculpatory and exculpatory) and treat complainants and respondents equally; decision-makers may analyze whether evidence warrants a high or low level of weight or credibility but must not automatically assign higher weight to exculpatory character evidence than to inculpatory character evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients cannot exclude relevant evidence solely because it concerns character or prior bad acts; §106.44(b)(2) assures the Department will refrain from second-guessing a recipient's determination of responsibility based solely on different weighing of evidence. Decision-makers should apply the same standards of relevance and weight to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rape-shield protections — sexual predisposition and prior sexual behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions and evidence about a complainant's sexual predisposition are never relevant; questions or evidence about a complainant's prior sexual behavior are not relevant except in two circumstances: (1) to prove someone other than the respondent committed the alleged misconduct, or (2) where the sexual behavior was between the complainant and respondent and is offered to prove consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not admit or use sexual predisposition evidence; evaluate prior sexual behavior only under the specified narrow exceptions. Decision-makers must exclude questions/evidence outside those exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privileged information protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The grievance process must prevent disclosure or use during a grievance process of information protected by a legally recognized privilege (added §106.45(b)(1)(x)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must identify and safeguard privileged communications consistent with law and not permit their disclosure in proceedings except where authorized by law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment records consent requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are barred from using a party's treatment records without the party's voluntary, written consent (revision to §106.45(b)(5)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not access or rely on medical or therapeutic treatment records unless the party has given written consent; treat such records as sensitive and protected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal application of additional rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any provisions, rules, or practices other than those required by §106.45 that a recipient adopts as part of its grievance process must apply equally to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional rules (e.g., decorum, timing, breaks) must be drafted and enforced in a manner that does not favor one party over the other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-examination must be conducted by advisors (no self-representation)
rubrics_metrics.description: In live hearings at postsecondary institutions, cross-examination is restricted to being conducted by a party's advisor; parties may not personally conduct cross-examination themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction is intended to reduce trauma and preserve the truth-seeking function of cross-examination. Parties retain the right not to participate, but if they wish to test credibility via cross-examination they must do so through an advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient-provided advisor when party lacks one
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party does not have an advisor present at the hearing, the recipient must provide without fee or charge to that party an advisor of the recipient's choice, who may be, but is not required to be, an attorney, to conduct cross-examination on behalf of that party (revision removing 'aligned with that party').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient has wide latitude in selecting the assigned advisor; the advisor's role is limited to conducting cross-examination on the party's behalf. The recipient cannot charge the party for the provided advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on restricting a party's choice or consultation with advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice or presence of a party's advisor cannot be limited by the recipient; recipients cannot forbid a party from conferring with their advisor, though recipients may adopt rules governing timing/length of breaks and decorum that apply equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may adopt reasonable, equally-applied rules about conduct and logistics, but cannot inhibit a party's access to their advisor or impose preconditions (such as fees) on advisors of choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisors' active participation limited except for cross-examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may limit the active participation of advisors in hearings, with the one exception that an advisor must be permitted to conduct cross-examination on behalf of a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may restrict advisor participation in non-cross-examination aspects (e.g., speaking on behalf of party) so long as the restriction is applied equally to both parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned advisors not subject to Title IX neutrality obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisors of choice and advisors provided by a recipient are not subject to the §106.45(b)(1)(iii) requirement that Title IX personnel serve impartially without conflicts of interest or bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisors may hold beliefs or loyalties; that does not change the recipient's obligation to have neutral decision-makers who objectively evaluate the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandated competency, prescreening, or training requirement for assigned advisors
rubrics_metrics.description: The final regulations decline to require recipients to prescreen a panel of assigned advisors, require assigned advisors to receive training, or require particular qualifications—recipients retain discretion to take such steps but are not required to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may train or vet employees they appoint as advisors, but the regulations do not impose an obligation to do so. The Department does, however, require decision-makers be trained specifically in issues of relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assigned advisor's role satisfied by relaying party's questions
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisor's cross-examination 'on behalf of that party' is satisfied where the advisor poses questions on a party's behalf, which means an assigned advisor could relay a party's own questions to the other party or witness; no particular skill or qualification is needed to perform that role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The function can be simply to serve as a proxy for the party's questions; recipients' compliance is objectively determined by whether the assigned advisor conducted cross-examination on the party's behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: No basis to challenge adequacy of assigned advisor
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims that a recipient provided ineffective assistance of counsel or an inadequate assigned advisor will not be entertained by the Department because the provision does not require advisors be lawyers or hold particular levels of skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties cannot successfully challenge outcomes solely on the basis that an assigned advisor was not 'adequate' under these regulations; the requirement is limited to performance of the advisor role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion when assigned advisor refuses or misconducts
rubrics_metrics.description: If a provided advisor refuses to comply with rules or refuses to conduct cross-examination on the party's behalf, the recipient may provide a different advisor or take other steps (including stopping the hearing to assign a new advisor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party cannot 'fire' an assigned advisor during the hearing; if the assigned advisor is not performing the required function, the recipient must ensure the party has an advisor to conduct cross-examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on charging fees for recipient-provided advisor and limits on fee restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients may not charge a party any fee for a recipient-provided advisor and may not impose training or competency assessments on advisors of choice selected by parties; recipients may, at their discretion, train their own employees who might be appointed as advisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must provide the assigned advisor without fee or charge; they may not condition provision on payment or preclude a party's paid advisor from participating due to cost restrictions (subject to equal application rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on accompanying persons and confidentiality constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties may not be accompanied to a live hearing by persons other than their advisors, except persons whose presence is required by law (e.g., disability aides, interpreters); §106.71 requires recipients to keep confidential the identity of individuals who report or are involved in sex discrimination proceedings, which may limit ability to authorize additional persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidentiality obligations under FERPA and §106.71 should guide decisions about who may attend; recipients should avoid permitting non-advisor third parties whose presence could violate confidentiality or the privacy of participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-makers must explain exclusions of questions as not relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Decision-makers are required to explain to the party's advisor posing a question any decision to exclude a question as not relevant (requirement referenced in §106.45(b)(6)(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explanation is intended to increase transparency and reduce perceived bias; commenters raised concerns about on-the-spot legal rulings, hearing length, and possible chilling effects on excluding rape-shield-protected questions. Recipients may consider written explanations after hearings as a practical alternative consistent with rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient neutrality and ability to enforce codes of conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must remain neutral and the decision-maker must serve impartially, but recipients retain the ability to enforce their own codes of conduct for non-Title IX matters and to take action if a party or advisor breaks recipient rules during a hearing, provided all §106.45 obligations are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional disciplinary steps for rule violations are permissible so long as grievance processes remain compliant with Title IX requirements and enforcement is even-handed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retaliation prohibition and confidentiality (§106.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: §106.71 prohibits retaliation: no recipient or other person may intimidate, threaten, coerce, or discriminate against any individual for exercising rights under Title IX or participating/refusing to participate in proceedings. Recipients must keep confidential the identity of complainants, respondents, witnesses, and reporters except as required by FERPA, other law, or to carry out Title IX purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must have policies and practices protecting participants from retaliation and preserving confidentiality to the extent legally permissible; confidentiality limits may affect who can attend hearings or be provided as advisors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stopping hearings to assign an advisor if needed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party appears at a hearing without an advisor, the recipient must stop the hearing as necessary to permit the recipient to assign an advisor to that party to conduct cross-examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should have procedures to promptly assign an advisor to avoid undue delay while ensuring parties' right to cross-examination via an advisor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient discretion on whether advisors may conduct direct examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether advisors may conduct direct examination is left to a recipient's discretion, though any rule restricting or permitting direct examination must apply equally to both parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should document their rule on direct examination and enforce it evenly; decision-makers must ensure relevance and equal application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility for recipients to provide attorney representation voluntarily
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the regulations precludes a recipient from offering to provide attorneys or non-attorney advisors to parties throughout the grievance process or for a live hearing, but the recipient cannot require a party to accept such representation and parties retain the right to select their own advisor of choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offering institutional attorneys is discretionary and must not interfere with parties' right to choose advisors; recipients may offer this service but should allow parties to refuse it.
